 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant in O.P (MV) No.595 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the appellant/claimant, on 13.10.2009 at about 12.45 am, while the petitioner was driving a tempo van, a LPG Tanker Lorry bearing registration No.KL-13-S-1843 driven by the 2nd respondent, which was moving infront of the tempo van, suddenly turned towards the right without any signal.
As a result of it, the tempo van going behind the tanker lorry happened to hit the back of the tanker lorry and thereby he sustained serious injuries.
The appellant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 13,00,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 and 2 remained ex parte.

The respondent insurer filed a written statement,
admitting the policy but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, oral testimony of PW1 was adduced on the side of the petitioner.
Exts.A1 to A15 were marked on the side of the appellant/claimant.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 5,25,500/- (50% of 10,51,000/-) as compensation under different heads with interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from respondent-insurer.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurance company.
5.
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal had found composite negligence on the part of the claimant in causing the accident.
The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that the charge sheet was drawn only against the driver of the tanker lorry and not against the driver of the tempo van.

6. The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the claimant himself has given evidence before the tribunal that while he was moving forward, the tanker lorry suddenly stopped, and since it was turned to the left side without giving any signal, the tempo van hit against the back of the tanker lorry and thus caused the accident.
The tribunal, on the basis MACA NO. 1594 OF 2014 2025:KER:39647 of the evidence given by PW1 found that there was composite negligence on the part of the claimant as well in causing the accident.
7. I have considered the rival contentions raised by both sides.
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has found that PW1 in his evidence admitted that the front portion of the tempo van had hit exactly on the rear side of the lorry.
The tribunal found that the tempo van driver was not keeping the safe distance which ought to have been maintained by the van while going behind the tanker lorry.

However, it is to be noted that PW1 deposed before the tribunal that the claimant,

sentences.text: It is true that the hit was on the rear side of the tanker lorry.
However, it is seen that the charge sheet was drawn only against the driver of the lorry and A charge and B charge were not raised in the case.

Considering the fact that hit was on the rear side of the lorry and no charge sheet drawn against the driver of the tempo van, I find that the percentage of composite negligence attributed by the tribunal can be reduced to 20:80, i.e., 20% on the part of the claimant in this appeal and 80% on the part of the insurer.
MACA NO. 1594 OF 2014 2025:KER:39647 Notional income :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 9,000/- was claimed by the appellant, the tribunal has taken only an amount of 5,000/- as the monthly income.
Following the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], I am inclined to refix the income of the appellant as 7,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Loss of earnings :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that towards the head loss of earnings, the tribunal has taken only a period of six months for awarding compensation.
Considering the fact that there was an amputation of one leg, I am inclined to grant a period of eight months for awarding compensation.
Since the notional monthly income is refixed at 7,000/-, the total compensation payable under the head is recalculated thus: 56,000/- (7,000x8).
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 30,000/- under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 26,000/- under the head loss of earnings.
Pain and sufferings :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 40,000/-.

Considering the fact that there was an amputation of one MACA NO.
1594 OF 2014 2025:KER:39647 leg, I find that a total amount of 60,000/- can be awarded under the head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 20,000/- under the afore head.
Compensation for permanent disability :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that no disability certificate was produced and that the tribunal has taken 45% disability as per the workmen's compensation Act.
The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that as per Schedule I of Workmen's Compensation Act, the percentage of disability for amputation below the knee is 50%.
Here the amputation is below the knee.
Accordingly, the tribunal ought to have taken the percentage of disability as 50%.
The learned counsel also submitted that since the claimant was a driver by profession, due to the amputation he has lost his job.
Considering his functional disability, I find that the percentage of functional disability can be fixed at 70%.
Since there is an amputation of one leg, I find that 25% of future prospects should be added to the notional income now fixed by this Court.
Therefore, the notional income for awarding compensation for disability will come to 8,750/- (7,000+7,000x25%).

Accordingly, the compensation payable under the head is recalculated thus:
11,02,500/- (8,750x12x15x70/100)).
The tribunal has already MACA NO. 1594 OF 2014 2025:KER:39647 awarded an amount of 4,05,000/- under the said head.
Thus there will be an additional amount of 6,97,500/- under the head compensation for disability.

The respondent insurer shall deposit the balance 30% of the original amount awarded by the tribunal as well as 80% of the enhanced amount now awarded by this Court together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.

Upon such deposit being made,
the MACA NO. 1594 OF 2014 2025:KER:39647 entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 342 days in filing the appeal.
